task_completion.description: Enclosed exterior walls and interior partition walls are drawn to create at least four distinct rooms.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 2D plan view shows a closed perimeter of thick lines (walls) with internal dividers creating separate spaces.

task_completion.description: Rooms are explicitly named: Living Room, Bedroom, Bathroom, and Kitchen.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Text labels or room floor area tags visible in the 2D plan view for all four required room names.

task_completion.description: At least one exterior door, two interior doors, and four windows are placed in the walls.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Door and window symbols (arcs for doors, rectangles for windows) integrated into the wall lines in the 2D plan.

task_completion.description: The cabin is furnished with a bed, sofa, table, four chairs, two kitchen appliances, a toilet, and a sink.
task_completion.visual_evidence: 3D models or 2D icons representing these specific items are visible within the room boundaries (e.g., bed in Bedroom, toilet in Bathroom).

task_completion.description: At least three dimension lines are placed to document clearances.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Lines with arrows and numerical distance values (e.g., '150 cm') placed on the plan to measure distances between walls or objects.

task_completion.description: The project is saved to the specific path ~/Documents/SweetHome3D/vacation_cabin.sh3d.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The Sweet Home 3D title bar shows 'vacation_cabin.sh3d' or the 'Save As' dialog box is seen with the correct path and filename typed in.

integrity.description: The agent used the Sweet Home 3D GUI to design the cabin rather than just creating a file via terminal.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with the wall tool, furniture catalog, and plan view within the Sweet Home 3D application window.

integrity.description: The design was built incrementally rather than appearing instantly from a pre-existing file.
integrity.visual_evidence: Sequential screenshots show the progression from an empty grid to walls, then doors/windows, then furniture.

integrity.description: The agent did not use a script to generate the .sh3d XML content directly.
integrity.visual_evidence: The agent is seen dragging items from the furniture list on the left into the plan area on the right.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The final design must be saved specifically to /home/ga/Documents/SweetHome3D/vacation_cabin.sh3d. The task is a creative design task; there is no pre-existing template, so the layout is valid as long as it contains the 4 named rooms, the specific furniture counts (1 bed, 1 sofa, 1 table, 4 chairs, 2 appliances, 1 toilet, 1 sink), and 3 dimension lines.
